# Clause 3 of I-0492: the widened route does not depend on the partitioned datum

Protection `I-0492` clause 3 says the chart-wise partitions of unity "have to go". The standing
measurement of that obligation (`I-0667`) is **33 textual `partition₀`/`partition₁` hits across 11
files**, which is a *file-level* count — and by `I-0678` (price a port by declaration reference,
not by import closure) a file-level count cannot decide the question, because a module can sit in
an import cone without a single declaration of the widened route referencing it.

This module answers it at the level that matters, in two forms.

## 1. As a dependency measurement

`#eval partitionAuditReport` walks the transitive constant-dependency closure of four widened
endpoints and of two chart-typed **controls**, and reports which of them mention the
`FinCoverData` carrier. Measured 2026-07-29 (run 0070 s0014):

| declaration | closure | mentions `FinCoverData`? |
|---|---|---|
| `exists_affAdaptation_isCertified_of_straddling` | 4270 | **no** |
| `exists_isCertified_of_swallowing_affineOpen` | 4270 | **no** |
| `AffAdaptation.isCertified_of_swallowedBy_of_c1` | 3860 | **no** |
| `divFamZarAff_of_forall_prime_certified_adaptation` | 3024 | **no** |
| CONTROL `DivisorAdaptation.ofChartPair` | 3897 | yes — `FinCoverData`, `.mk`, `.pieces` |
| CONTROL `chartPairCoverData` | 3863 | yes — `FinCoverData`, `.mk` |

**Read the controls first.** A probe reporting "absent" on both sides measures nothing, and the
first version of this one did exactly that: it searched for the FIELD names
`partition₀`/`partition₁`/`cover₀`/`cover₁` and came back empty *including on the controls*. The
reason is worth keeping — a producer builds the structure with `FinCoverData.mk`, so the field name
never occurs in the term. **A structure field is not a constant a proof term mentions.** Probing
the carrier and its constructor makes the controls fire, and only then does a clean reading on the
widened side license a conclusion. This is trap (c) of `I-0442` in dependency form: uncalibrated
absence and real absence print identically.

## 2. As a theorem

A dependency walk is evidence about *proof terms*, which no `#print axioms` and no build can check
for you. So the mathematical content is also stated as an ordinary theorem:
`isCertified_widened_of_isCertified_widened_partitionFree` records that the widened certificate
predicate is preserved under replacing the cover by any other widened cover carrying the same
adaptation data — i.e. the certificate never inspects how the cover was *produced*, which is what
"partition-free" means for a consumer. It is proved by `id`, and that is the point: there is
nothing to transport, because `AffCoverData` carries no partition to begin with.

## What this does NOT say

It does **not** say the 49-file consumer migration of `I-0667` is unnecessary. The two
measurements answer different questions: that count is about which carrier the *consumers* use,
this one about whether the widened *route* depends on the partitioned datum. Both can be true.

/-- The transitive constant-dependency closure of `start`, following both a declaration's TYPE and
its `value?` (where a theorem's proof term lives).

Named `depClosure` rather than `closure`: with `AlgebraicJacobian` open, `closure` collides with
the topological closure and the collision is reported as a baffling `TopologicalSpace Name`
instance failure. -/
def depClosure (env : Environment) (start : Name) : NameSet := Id.run do
  let mut seen : NameSet := {}
  let mut stack := [start]
  while !stack.isEmpty do
    let n := stack.head!
    stack := stack.tail!
    if seen.contains n then continue
    seen := seen.insert n
    if let some ci := env.find? n then
      let mut cs : NameSet := ci.type.getUsedConstants.foldl (·.insert ·) {}
      if let some v := ci.value? then
        cs := v.getUsedConstants.foldl (·.insert ·) cs
      for c in cs.toList do
        if !seen.contains c then stack := c :: stack

## ADDENDUM 10 (2026-07-29, run 0070 session 0014) — the widening is proved STRICT, and clause 3 is measured at the DECLARATION level (BINDING; sharpens ADDENDUM 9 §9.4 and I-0667)

Three results, in descending order of how much they change the lane's status.

### 10.1 The four modules of ADDENDUM 9 are now kernel-green, and TWO of them were WRONG

ADDENDUM 9 §9.1a recorded one module green and three "fixed but not re-checked", and `I-0675`
filed that as a live hazard. All four are now verified (`lean -o`, `EXIT=0`, zero diagnostics), and
the check was worth running because **two carried real proof errors that no sorry census, job count
or `ls-tree` readback could see**:

* `DivisorFamilyAffFunctorCompare.lean:78` — the two backward rewrites of
  `DivFamZar.toAff_mapAlgHom` were placed *before* `divFamZarToAffVehicle_val`, so on the
  right-hand side there was no `_.toAff` spelling for them to match. The reported symptom was
  *"the target expression is not type-correct under the `instances` transparency level"*, which
  reads like a broken goal and is nothing of the kind — the fix is to let the forward rewrite
  normalise the spelling first.
* `DivRepGlobalAffLift.lean:145` — after the transport, `pullGlobalAff_comp`'s two sides were equal
  only up to unfolding the folded name `pullGlobalAff`; `rw`'s terminal `rfl` runs at reducible
  transparency and cannot see a plain `def`. One explicit `rfl`.

Also removed there: a redundant `[IsAffineHom pi]` binder that `[IsFinite pi]` already implies,
which had every declaration in the file emitting an overlapping-instance warning.

**Method note, and it matters under lane contention.** The check used `lean -o` writing into a
scratch olean tree seeded by *symlinks* to the project's `.lake` oleans. That writes no shared
build state, so it needs **no lake mutex** (protocol §5b) and cost ~18 s per module against a
queued `lake build` that had previously burned 3300 s and timed out.

### 10.2 THE PAYOFF IS NOW A THEOREM: the widening is strict

Everything the lane had built established that the widened carrier is *well-formed and usable*.
Nothing established that it **buys** anything. The claim that it does appeared only as prose —
`DivisorFamilyAffCompare.lean:249` says "the converse is FALSE, and that failure is the content of
R2" — while both of its halves had been landed theorems for days. `Picard/DivisorFamilyAffStrict.lean`
composes them:

    isCertified_affine_and_not_isCertified_chart
      -- at ONE divisor, ONE degree, ONE base:
      --   (∃ widened cover + adaptation) certified at n
      --   ∧ ∀ chart-typed adaptation, ∀ degree, NOT certified

This is the R2 justification in the form a reviewer can check. Per `reduction-needs-its-converse`,
`isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_isLocallyCertified` was a `≤` and a `≤` is only a *strict* widening once
something is exhibited on the far side; this exhibits it. **No hypothesis on `|P¹(k)|` occurs in
either half** — which is the field-uniformity R2 was chosen for over a field-size hypothesis.

**Scope, and it is stated in the file rather than only here.** The separation is CONDITIONAL and is
**not** certified non-vacuous. The witness exists mathematically over every field including `F₂`
(§4.3), but formalising it is out of scope by §4.5 — it needs `Sym^g C` with its universal flat
divisor. Critically, the lane's existing `n = 0` non-vacuity witnesses **do not** inhabit these
hypotheses: they sit at an *empty* support locus, and a straddling divisor has nonempty support by
the very witnesses `hx`/`hy` that make it straddle. That had to be said explicitly, because a
reader who knows the endpoint has a non-vacuity witness would otherwise assume it transfers.

### 10.3 Clause 3 is discharged ON THE WIDENED ROUTE, and the 33-hit count answers a different question

`I-0667` and ADDENDUM 9's closing paragraph price clause 3 as 33 textual `partition₀`/`partition₁`
hits across 11 files. That is a **file-level** measurement, and by `I-0678` (price a port by
declaration reference, not by import closure) it cannot decide whether the widened route *depends*
on the partitioned datum. `scripts/partition-probe.lean` walks the transitive constant-dependency
closure and answers it:

| declaration | closure | depends on `FinCoverData`? |
|---|---|---|
| `exists_affAdaptation_isCertified_of_straddling` | 4270 | **no** |
| `exists_isCertified_of_swallowing_affineOpen` | 4270 | **no** |
| `AffAdaptation.isCertified_of_swallowedBy_of_c1` | 3860 | **no** |
| `divFamZarAff_of_forall_prime_certified_adaptation` | 3024 | **no** |
| CONTROL `DivisorAdaptation.ofChartPair` | 3897 | yes — `FinCoverData`, `.mk`, `.pieces` |
| CONTROL `chartPairCoverData` | 3863 | yes — `FinCoverData`, `.mk` |

So the widened certificate route is partition-free where it counts, and the 33 hits live in files no
declaration of that route reaches. This does **not** say the 49-file migration is unnecessary — it
says the two measurements answer different questions, and that the 33 hits are not a blocker on the
widened route.

**The calibration failure is the part to carry forward.** The first version of that probe searched
for the FIELD names `partition₀`/`partition₁`/`cover₀`/`cover₁` and reported EMPTY *on both sides,
including the control that must fire*. Cause: a producer builds the structure with
`FinCoverData.mk`, so the field name never occurs in the term — **a structure field is not a
constant a proof term mentions.** Probing the carrier and its constructor makes the control fire,
and only a probe whose control fires can license a negative conclusion. This is trap (c) of `I-0442`
in dependency form: uncalibrated absence and real absence print identically.

### 10.4 What the lane still owes

Unchanged and still exactly one geometric statement: the subordinate **Stacks `0B8B`** input
(`I-0565` half (a)), assumed per I-0492 clause 2. Obligation 4(i) stays discharged (ADDENDUM 7) and
4(ii) is the joint-cover field of `AffCoverData` (ADDENDUM 5). The 49-file consumer migration is
open but is now known not to gate the widened route's own correctness.

---
name: lock-free-kernel-check-scratch-oleans
description: Kernel-check a Lean module without the shared build lock by symlinking existing oleans into a scratch LEAN_PATH root — 18s per module vs a queued build, and it caught two real errors a sorry census could not.
metadata:
  type: reference
---

To kernel-check one or a few Lean modules when a shared `lake` mutex is held by another lane
(AJCR's is `/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock`, a mkdir DIRECTORY lock), do **not** queue a
`lake build`. Write oleans into a scratch tree instead — it touches no shared build state, so the
protocol's lock does not apply (concurrent-lane protocol §5b explicitly permits the narrowest
check):

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/scratch-oleans
REAL=.lake/build/lib/lean
# seed the scratch root with SYMLINKS to every existing olean
for o in $(cd $REAL && find <RootModuleDir> -name '*.olean'); do
  mkdir -p /tmp/scratch-oleans/$(dirname $o)
  ln -s "$(realpath $REAL/$o)" "/tmp/scratch-oleans/$o"
done
LP=$(lake env printenv LEAN_PATH)
export LEAN_PATH="/tmp/scratch-oleans:$LP"
lean -o /tmp/scratch-oleans/<Path>/<Mod>.olean <Path>/<Mod>.lean; echo "EXIT=$?"
```

Three traps, all hit on the first attempt:

- **`lake env lean` overwrites your `LEAN_PATH`.** Use plain `lean` after exporting it, or the
  scratch root is silently dropped and you get "object file ... does not exist".
- **Lean resolves each module against the FIRST matching root only**, so an unseeded scratch root
  makes every already-built dependency look absent. Hence the symlink seeding — cheap, no copying.
- Build the chain in dependency order and write each module's olean into the scratch root, so the
  next module in the chain can find it.

Cost measured 2026-07-29: ~18 s per module, against a `lake build` of the same target that had
previously burned 3300 s and hit its timeout under 8-lane contention.

**Why it is worth doing rather than deferring.** Applied to four modules a predecessor had
committed unverified, it found **two real proof errors** that no sorry census, job count or
`git ls-tree` readback could see — see [[binder-hides-work-from-a-sorry-census]] and
[[rfl-equal-spellings-block-rw]] for the two shapes. A module can be sorry-free, rooted, and red.

Limitation to state honestly in a report: this checks the named modules against *existing* oleans
for their dependencies. It is a faithful kernel check of those files, but it is not evidence that
the whole project builds, and it will not notice that a dependency's olean is stale — cross-check

Never land a file with `git add -f`. If the ignore rule refuses your path, that refusal is the
answer: either the artefact is throwaway (leave it untracked and don't cite it), or it has earned a
place in the library and belongs under the source tree with a real module name.

**Why:** AJCR's `.gitignore` ignores `*Probe*.lean` / `*probe*.lean` precisely because a probe
created and deleted across sessions otherwise "haunts the tree forever afterwards as a phantom
staged deletion". A probe I force-added hit exactly that: `git add` refused it, so the standard
disarm recipe (`reset -- <path>`, see [[cas-commit-arms-the-shared-index]]) could never clear it, it

symptom as a concurrency incident **twice** before a hygiene pass found the ignore rule — see
